criteria.rationale: Unmet clause: when an entity with the same identity is in two consecutive steps, navigating between them must animate it from its old state to its new state in place. The kit's Arrow entity primitive fails this when the two steps do not share a scene group. How the failure happens: - sceneKey gives an ungrouped step the key `step:${step.id}`. Stage therefore mounts a new keyed scene motion.div inside AnimatePresence (default sync mode, position:absolute, inset:0). The outgoing scene fades out over ENTER_T = 0.4s. - In the incoming scene, Arrow mounts with initial opacity 0. Its animate transition has delay ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, then a 0.4s fade. - Arrow has no layoutId or layout prop. Its path `d` values start at the new path (initial = animate = paths.line). - So an arrow with the same id in both steps is fully faded out with the outgoing scene by 0.4s. It stays invisible until 0.6s and then fades in at its new geometry. It vanishes and reappears instead of morphing. - This is the guidance's second named failure pattern: both steps stay mounted while the entity primitive hides the incoming copy, with a fixed initial opacity of 0 and an entrance delay at least as long as the step transition. Arrow counts as a kit entity primitive. It is exported by the kit, takes a required `id`, and renders it as `data-presentation-entity`. The delivered sample also uses it to render identified entities (LINES with E.* ids). Judge A (fail) is borne out by Arrow.tsx, Stage.tsx, sceneKey.ts and constants.ts, and its reason decides the requirement. Judges B and C (pass) are each right that sync mode with an out-of-flow scene wrapper keeps both scenes mounted. They are also right that LayoutNode (used by Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip) has a layoutId and no opacity hiding, so those entities can morph. But both judges assessed only LayoutNode-based primitives. B even notes that the newcomer delay 'lives only in Appear (enter prop) and Arrow' without seeing that Arrow has no `enter` opt-out and no layoutId. That means every Arrow in a freshly mounted ungrouped scene is treated as a newcomer. Morphing for some primitives does not meet the requirement for an arrow entity, which disappears and reappears.

subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: computeFitScale returns one scalar, min(w/canvas.width, h/canvas.height), applied as scale(s) on both axes to a fixed-size canvas. It is measured from the stage element's own rect, which excludes the header, footer, attribution and ToC. The canvas is not reflowed, only transformed.
evidence: fit.ts computeFitScale: scale = Math.min(w / canvas.width, h / canvas.height), clamped to [MIN_SCALE 0.2, MAX_SCALE 2], with per-mode padding from STAGE_LAYOUT.
useFitScale.ts measures el.getBoundingClientRect() of the stage ref and re-measures with a ResizeObserver.
Stage.tsx: the canvas has fixed width/height and transform: translate(-50%,-50%) scale(${scale}), inside an overflow:hidden stage.
At 390x844 the stage is about 390 wide, so w = 390-2*16 = 358 (browse) or 390-96 = 294 (present). The scale is about 0.41 or 0.33, so the canvas is about 358 or 294 wide, which fits the stage width.
At 1280x720 the stage height is the root height minus the chrome, and the scale follows that measured height. Because the fit comes from the stage rect, the canvas stays inside the stage.
judging basis: consensus-pass

But those two scenarios do not cover the guidance's 'steps content absent' case, which still ends in a render timeout. So their reasoning does not show the requirement is fully met.

criteria.rationale: The preview is a spawned `vite.js preview` process, and `stop()` in preview.mjs only sends SIGTERM to its process group. It never awaits the child's exit. The requirement is to terminate and await the server process itself. In inspect-presentation.mjs, `chromium.launch()` runs outside the try/finally, so a browser launch failure skips `preview.stop()`. result.rationale: Unmet clause: when an entity with the same identity is in two consecutive steps, navigating between them must animate it from its old state to its new state in place. The kit's Arrow entity primitive fails this when the two steps do not share a scene group. How the failure happens: - sceneKey gives an ungrouped step the key `step:${step.id}`. Stage therefore mounts a new keyed scene motion.div inside AnimatePresence (default sync mode, position:absolute, inset:0). The outgoing scene fades out over ENTER_T = 0.4s. - In the incoming scene, Arrow mounts with initial opacity 0. Its animate transition has delay ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, then a 0.4s fade. - Arrow has no layoutId or layout prop. Its path `d` values start at the new path (initial = animate = paths.line). - So an arrow with the same id in both steps is fully faded out with the outgoing scene by 0.4s. It stays invisible until 0.6s and then fades in at its new geometry. It vanishes and reappears instead of morphing. - This is the guidance's second named failure pattern: both steps stay mounted while the entity primitive hides the incoming copy, with a fixed initial opacity of 0 and an entrance delay at least as long as the step transition. Arrow counts as a kit entity primitive. It is exported by the kit, takes a required `id`, and renders it as `data-presentation-entity`. The delivered sample also uses it to render identified entities (LINES with E.* ids). Judge A (fail) is borne out by Arrow.tsx, Stage.tsx, sceneKey.ts and constants.ts, and its reason decides the requirement. Judges B and C (pass) are each right that sync mode with an out-of-flow scene wrapper keeps both scenes mounted. They are also right that LayoutNode (used by Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip) has a layoutId and no opacity hiding, so those entities can morph. But both judges assessed only LayoutNode-based primitives. B even notes that the newcomer delay 'lives only in Appear (enter prop) and Arrow' without seeing that Arrow has no `enter` opt-out and no layoutId. That means every Arrow in a freshly mounted ungrouped scene is treated as a newcomer. Morphing for some primitives does not meet the requirement for an arrow entity, which disappears and reappears.

result.rationale: The guidance counts a sample as missing when it is not registered, or when its outline or steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent or out of order. It requires the verifier to fail at a check that reports the sample as missing or not matching the outline. A failure that only shows up later as a browser or render timeout does not count. The verifier has only one check that runs before rendering: sampleRegistryPhase (scripts/verify.mjs:58-65). It only looks for the slug among the registered slugs. main() (verify.mjs:152-159) runs only the build, that slug check, a check that some presentation is registered, and the render phase. Nothing reads the sample's steps or outline before the browser starts. The step-count, title and caption checks (verify.mjs:88-106) all run after the page has shown [data-presentation-root] (verify.mjs:82-86). Now take the case where all steps content is absent but the slug is still registered. That means STEPS is empty and the step imports are gone too, so this is a complete removal, not the partial deletion the guidance excludes. The registry still loads Talk (src/presentations/index.ts:10-16; App.tsx:17-29). Talk passes STEPS to Presentation (Talk.tsx:1-7; steps/index.ts:12). An empty AnyStep[] is still valid for the type checker under tsconfig.app.json, so the build has nothing to reject. buildOutline turns an empty array into empty entries (outline.ts:4-16). Presentation then returns null because entries[0] is undefined (Presentation.tsx:33-37), so [data-presentation-root] never appears. After the 4000 ms wait the verifier throws VerifyError('render', 'presentation root [data-presentation-root] did not render') (verify.mjs:11, 82-86). It prints 'FAIL phase=render' (verify.mjs:161-171), which is a render timeout, not a sample or outline check. The sample-phase step-count check at line 91 is never reached. The tests (tests/e2e/verify-failures.test.ts:37-70) cover only the unregistered case and the out-of-order case. Nothing covers absent steps content. Judge B named this gap, and the code bears it out. Judges A and C are right that an unregistered or reordered sample fails with 'FAIL phase=sample'. It only looks for the slug among the registered slugs. main() (verify.mjs:152-159) runs only the build, that slug check, a check that some presentation is registered, and the render phase. The step-count, title and caption checks (verify.mjs:88-106) all run after the page has shown [data-presentation-root] (verify.mjs:82-86). Now take the case where all steps content is absent but the slug is still registered. votes.rationale: The port is ephemeral and passed with --strictPort, but readiness comes only from HTTP polling of that port. checks.rationale: The dissent says the browser-backed tests use fixed settling sleeps. The cited material does not show that. vitest.integration.config.ts limits the browser-backed tests to tests/integration/** and tests/e2e/**. None of those test files contains a sleep or waitForTimeout. None treats an instant read as if it waited. Each one runs verify or inspect through `sh()` in tests/helpers/materialize.ts, which wraps `spawnSync`. The assertions run only after the child process has exited, so they check finished, observable output: exit code, log lines, the manifest, and whether the preview port still answers. The `page.waitForTimeout` calls the dissent cites are in the verification tooling (scripts/verify.mjs and the bootstrap inspect-presentation.mjs), not in a delivered test. Even inside that tooling, each step change is awaited with a polling `waitForFunction` on `data-step-index` with a timeout, and verify checks the index before the settle delay. The settle is a documented capture delay, not a stand-in for waiting on state. INT-002 asserts `capturedAt - navigatedAt >= settle`, but that reads a manifest the finished process wrote; the test itself does not sleep. The jsdom unit tests are not browser tests, and they also use polling `waitFor` with timeouts. So the dissent's facts do not show any clause of the requirement unmet, and the majority's pass reasoning stands.

votes.rationale: The tests never hardcode a port. The scripts they run allocate one through `freePort()` (a `listen(0)` call) and pass `--port` to vite preview with `--strictPort`. The test processes run synchronously through `spawnSync`, and each test uses its own temp directory. Tests also assert the preview is gone afterwards: verify-pass.test.ts and verify-failures.test.ts both check that fetching the preview URL rejects. No test kills only an npm or npx wrapper; the scripts' `stop()` signals the whole process group of the spawned vite process.

first_results.rationale: Unmet clause: when an entity with the same identity is in two consecutive steps, navigating between them must animate it from its old state to its new state in place. The kit's Arrow entity primitive fails this when the two steps do not share a scene group. How the failure happens: - sceneKey gives an ungrouped step the key `step:${step.id}`. Stage therefore mounts a new keyed scene motion.div inside AnimatePresence (default sync mode, position:absolute, inset:0). The outgoing scene fades out over ENTER_T = 0.4s. - In the incoming scene, Arrow mounts with initial opacity 0. Its animate transition has delay ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, then a 0.4s fade. - Arrow has no layoutId or layout prop. Its path `d` values start at the new path (initial = animate = paths.line). - So an arrow with the same id in both steps is fully faded out with the outgoing scene by 0.4s. It stays invisible until 0.6s and then fades in at its new geometry. It vanishes and reappears instead of morphing. - This is the guidance's second named failure pattern: both steps stay mounted while the entity primitive hides the incoming copy, with a fixed initial opacity of 0 and an entrance delay at least as long as the step transition. Arrow counts as a kit entity primitive. It is exported by the kit, takes a required `id`, and renders it as `data-presentation-entity`. The delivered sample also uses it to render identified entities (LINES with E.* ids). Judge A (fail) is borne out by Arrow.tsx, Stage.tsx, sceneKey.ts and constants.ts, and its reason decides the requirement. Judges B and C (pass) are each right that sync mode with an out-of-flow scene wrapper keeps both scenes mounted. They are also right that LayoutNode (used by Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip) has a layoutId and no opacity hiding, so those entities can morph. But both judges assessed only LayoutNode-based primitives. B even notes that the newcomer delay 'lives only in Appear (enter prop) and Arrow' without seeing that Arrow has no `enter` opt-out and no layoutId. That means every Arrow in a freshly mounted ungrouped scene is treated as a newcomer. Morphing for some primitives does not meet the requirement for an arrow entity, which disappears and reappears.
evidence: src/presentation-kit/sceneKey.ts:16 returns `step:${step.id}` when a step has no groupKey, so consecutive ungrouped steps get distinct keys and Stage mounts separate scene subtrees.

results.rationale: Unmet clause: when an entity with the same identity is in two consecutive steps, navigating between them must animate it from its old state to its new state in place. The kit's Arrow entity primitive fails this when the two steps do not share a scene group. How the failure happens: - sceneKey gives an ungrouped step the key `step:${step.id}`. Stage therefore mounts a new keyed scene motion.div inside AnimatePresence (default sync mode, position:absolute, inset:0). The outgoing scene fades out over ENTER_T = 0.4s. - In the incoming scene, Arrow mounts with initial opacity 0. Its animate transition has delay ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, then a 0.4s fade. - Arrow has no layoutId or layout prop. Its path `d` values start at the new path (initial = animate = paths.line). - So an arrow with the same id in both steps is fully faded out with the outgoing scene by 0.4s. It stays invisible until 0.6s and then fades in at its new geometry. It vanishes and reappears instead of morphing. - This is the guidance's second named failure pattern: both steps stay mounted while the entity primitive hides the incoming copy, with a fixed initial opacity of 0 and an entrance delay at least as long as the step transition. Arrow counts as a kit entity primitive. It is exported by the kit, takes a required `id`, and renders it as `data-presentation-entity`. The delivered sample also uses it to render identified entities (LINES with E.* ids). Judge A (fail) is borne out by Arrow.tsx, Stage.tsx, sceneKey.ts and constants.ts, and its reason decides the requirement. Judges B and C (pass) are each right that sync mode with an out-of-flow scene wrapper keeps both scenes mounted. They are also right that LayoutNode (used by Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip) has a layoutId and no opacity hiding, so those entities can morph. But both judges assessed only LayoutNode-based primitives. B even notes that the newcomer delay 'lives only in Appear (enter prop) and Arrow' without seeing that Arrow has no `enter` opt-out and no layoutId. That means every Arrow in a freshly mounted ungrouped scene is treated as a newcomer. Morphing for some primitives does not meet the requirement for an arrow entity, which disappears and reappears.

audit_results.rationale: The criterion requires an entity that keeps the same identity across two consecutive ungrouped steps to animate in place from its old state to its new state. The quoted kit source shows that the Arrow entity primitive does not do this. - sceneKey.ts:16 gives each ungrouped step its own key, `step:${step.id}`. Stage.tsx:39-50 therefore mounts a new scene motion.div whenever the step changes. It sits inside a sync-mode AnimatePresence and is positioned out of flow (absolute, inset 0). The old scene fades out over ENTER_T = 0.4s (constants.ts:9). - In the new scene, Arrow.tsx:44-45 starts at opacity 0 and waits ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s (constants.ts:8,11) before fading in over 0.4s. - Arrow has no `layout` or `layoutId` (Arrow.tsx:36-48), so nothing carries its old state across the two scenes. - Its path `d` values start at the new geometry (`initial={{ d: paths.line }} animate={{ d: paths.line }}`, lines 50-53), so a newly mounted Arrow has no old geometry to animate from. The result: an arrow with the same id fades out with the old scene by 0.4s, stays invisible until 0.6s, then fades in at its new position. It vanishes and reappears instead of morphing. The review guidance names this as a failure: both steps stay mounted while the primitive hides the incoming copy behind an initial opacity of 0 and an entrance delay at least as long as the step transition. Arrow counts as a kit entity primitive. It takes a required `id` and renders it as `data-presentation-entity` (Arrow.tsx:6,38), and the sample renders identified entities through it (SampleScene.tsx:70-79, 96-98). LayoutNode-based primitives (LayoutNode.tsx:16-19) do morph through layoutId. That does not fix the Arrow case, because the requirement covers any entity with a persisting identity. The unmet clause, "animates that entity from its old state ... to its new state in place", is shown to be unmet for arrow entities across ungrouped steps.

first_results.rationale: The review guidance says a missing sample includes the case where the reference presentation is registered but its steps content is absent. That case must fail at a check that reports the sample as missing or not matching the outline. A failure that only shows up later as a browser or render timeout does not count. The verifier does not meet this. sampleRegistryPhase (scripts/verify.mjs:58-65) only checks that the slug string appears in src/presentations/index.ts. It never checks that the sample's steps, titles, or captions exist before rendering. The title, caption and step-count checks all run inside stepThrough, and only after page.waitForSelector('[data-presentation-root]') succeeds (verify.mjs:82-93). If the registered sample's STEPS array (steps/index.ts:12) has no entries, buildOutline (outline.ts:4-16) returns no entries. Presentation then hits `if (!entry) return null` (Presentation.tsx:33-37), so data-presentation-root never renders. The waitForSelector call times out, and the verifier reports 'FAIL phase=render ... presentation root [data-presentation-root] did not render' (verify.mjs:85). That is a render timeout, not a sample-phase report, which is exactly the outcome the guidance excludes. This matches Judge B's reason, and that reason decides the criterion. Judge A and Judge C correctly show that an unregistered slug fails with 'FAIL phase=sample ... is not registered' (verify.mjs:61-62; test at verify-failures.test.ts:37-44). They also show that out-of-order titles fail with phase=sample (verify.mjs:104-105; test at verify-failures.test.ts:61-70). Neither judge addresses absent steps content in a registered sample. That is part of the guidance's definition of a missing sample, and it ends in a render timeout. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met.

results.rationale: The guidance counts a sample as missing when it is not registered, or when its outline or steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent or out of order. It requires the verifier to fail at a check that reports the sample as missing or not matching the outline. A failure that only shows up later as a browser or render timeout does not count. The verifier has only one check that runs before rendering: sampleRegistryPhase (scripts/verify.mjs:58-65). It only looks for the slug among the registered slugs. main() (verify.mjs:152-159) runs only the build, that slug check, a check that some presentation is registered, and the render phase. Nothing reads the sample's steps or outline before the browser starts. The step-count, title and caption checks (verify.mjs:88-106) all run after the page has shown [data-presentation-root] (verify.mjs:82-86). Now take the case where all steps content is absent but the slug is still registered. That means STEPS is empty and the step imports are gone too, so this is a complete removal, not the partial deletion the guidance excludes. The registry still loads Talk (src/presentations/index.ts:10-16; App.tsx:17-29). Talk passes STEPS to Presentation (Talk.tsx:1-7; steps/index.ts:12). An empty AnyStep[] is still valid for the type checker under tsconfig.app.json, so the build has nothing to reject. buildOutline turns an empty array into empty entries (outline.ts:4-16). Presentation then returns null because entries[0] is undefined (Presentation.tsx:33-37), so [data-presentation-root] never appears. After the 4000 ms wait the verifier throws VerifyError('render', 'presentation root [data-presentation-root] did not render') (verify.mjs:11, 82-86). It prints 'FAIL phase=render' (verify.mjs:161-171), which is a render timeout, not a sample or outline check. The sample-phase step-count check at line 91 is never reached. The tests (tests/e2e/verify-failures.test.ts:37-70) cover only the unregistered case and the out-of-order case. Nothing covers absent steps content. Judge B named this gap, and the code bears it out. Judges A and C are right that an unregistered or reordered sample fails with 'FAIL phase=sample'. But those two scenarios do not cover the guidance's 'steps content absent' case, which still ends in a render timeout. So their reasoning does not show the requirement is fully met.
